sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Internet Retailing of Outdoor Sports and Camping Gear

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic; French commercial law heritage; unitary national legal system with no sub-state tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-United States DTA (1996, as amended by the 2004 Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Law of 25 March 2020 implementing EU sanctions; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS; UBO threshold per Art. 1(11) of the 2019 RBE Law: more than 25% of shares, voting rights or capital interests, directly or indirectly.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Incumbency, and Certificate of Good Standing of the foreign corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the general partner's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Luxembourg is party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961; consular legalization only for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney from the general partner and each limited partner appointing the Luxembourg manager, resident agent, and counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized true copies of passports plus proof of residential address of each UBO and the authorized signatories of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: SCSp partnership agreement (English original with certified French translation for RCS filing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg counsel and sworn translator; notarial form required only if real estate is contributed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization only if the notarial form is legally required; otherwise apostille of signature pages of foreign partners

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and corporate beneficial ownership chain chart (extracting the UBO register of the parent entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Overseas banks/group compliance and the foreign company registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for non-EU origin documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based KYC/AML file for all UBOs, the general partner, and its directors; PEP screening pursuant to FATF Recommendations 12 and 22 and Art. 3(11) of the 2004 AML Law; screening of UBOs, managers, counterparties, and payment processors (Stripe/PayPal) against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions, Luxembourg FIU (CRF) indicators, and OFAC SDN/50% rule lists for USD-clearing exposure; ongoing transaction monitoring and negative-news review; enhanced due diligence required when a UBO is a PEP, a sanction-designated person, or a high-risk jurisdiction customer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), electronic name-search portal at www.lbr.lu, with e-filing via the eJustice RCS module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in Latin characters and in a language accepted by the RCS (French, German, Luxembourgish or another Latin-script EU language); an English proposed name is permissible, but the SCSp deed and any certified French translation filed with the RCS must be in one of the statutory filing languages; the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS entry and must not mislead as to the legal form or the business activity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The proposed name is pre-checked on the LBR portal before filing; if rejected, the applicant receives a written RCS notification with the grounds for refusal; the applicant may file a written administrative objection with the RCS registrar within 30 calendar days, request an extraordinary clearance from the competent minister or professional body for sensitive tokens, and may subsequently apply to the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg (chambre commerciale) for judicial review; a new name can be submitted immediately without waiting for the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for the SCSp provided the registered address is hosted by an approved domiciliation agent under the Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies; appropriate for administrative and registration purposes only. Pure letterbox arrangements do not constitute commercial substance and create tax residency and permanent establishment risk under Art. 159 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (L.I.R.) and EU ATAD/anti-abuse rules. For an internet retail business, the contract management, books and records, bank account, and management decisions should be located in Luxembourg; the commercial risk profile remains Low_Risk_Standard.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 5-10% annual risk of an unannounced physical inspection by the RCS, the Social Security Centre (CCSS), or the tax administration; the risk rises to approximately 15% if the SCSp shows shell indicators such as no tax return, foreign management, unexplained related-party flows, or successive domiciliation changes within 12 months.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search and pre-clearance on LBR/RCS portal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed administrative tariff applicable at the LBR/RCS portal

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the SCSp partnership agreement (English), including statutory and AML annexes
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a private partnership deed (EUR 2,300 - 3,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of the SCSp partnership agreement for RCS filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory sworn-translator tariff per page (market benchmark)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille of foreign corporate general partner documents (certificate of incumbency, POA, passports, proof of address)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and competent apostille authority in the country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff plus Hague Apostille fixed fee (non-Luxembourg authority rates)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration filing and RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations) publication
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS filing and publication fees (approximately EUR 100 - 110)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC file preparation, PEP and sanctions screening of UBOs and general partner
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm and compliance database provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for standard PEP/sanctions/negative-news screening of two UBO levels

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Appointment of approved domiciliation agent and registered office service (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Domiciliation agent approved under the Law of 31 May 1999

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence and regulatory clearance review (tax substance, e-commerce licences, privacy, and payment processor rules)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for transactional due diligence package (EUR 3,500 - 4,200)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended; Article 23-2 et seq. (SCSp regime introduced by Law of 12 July 2013); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS Law); Law of 2 September 2011 on the Freedom of Establishment and Provision of Services.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), administered by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via the eService/rcs.lu online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration en vue de l'inscription au Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (Application for RCS Registration), accompanied by the signed Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société) and annexes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital requirement for an SCSp; capital is freely determined in the partnership agreement and may be contributed in cash, in-kind, or as services. No escrowed bank account (compte bloqué) or bank certificate is required by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: We, the sole General Partner of [SCSp], a Société en Commandite Spéciale governed by the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915, as amended, hereby resolve: (1) The Partnership Agreement is adopted and the capital contribution of each partner is subscribed as set out in Schedule A; (2) The registered office is fixed at [Address], Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, where corporate records are kept; (3) [Name] is appointed Managing Partner (Gérant) with full authority to represent, bind and administer the partnership, to open bank accounts, and to sign tax returns; (4) The Managing Partner is instructed to register the partnership with the RCS, arrange RESA publication, and complete all Luxembourg administrative formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the SCSp Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding partners; optional Luxembourg notary (mandatory only if real property is contributed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and sign the partnership agreement setting out the corporate name, partners' contributions, profit-sharing, identity of the general partner (associé commandité) and limited partners (associés commanditaires), management powers, and registered office clause. A private deed is sufficient for a fully cash-funded SCSp; a notarial deed is required for contributions of real estate. Obtain prior non-opposition/name clearance from the RCS before signing.
required_dossiers: Partnership agreement (original private deed or notarial act)
Identity documents (ID/passport) of all partners and the managing partner
Declaration of non-bankruptcy for each natural-person general partner
If corporate general partner: official RCS extract of the corporate partner
Proposed company name availability report from RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS flags a name conflict or legal-form non-compliance, amend and re-execute the partnership agreement, reserve an alternative company name, and submit a corrected filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation application with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the RCS registration application electronically through the LBR eService portal, attaching the signed partnership agreement, proof of registered office (lease or owner's written consent), and identity documents. Pay the applicable filing fee online; the partnership becomes legally existing upon registration and issuance of the RCS extract.
required_dossiers: Completed RCS registration form (déclaration d'inscription)
Signed partnership agreement
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or notarized owner consent)
Identity documents and criminal record extract of the managing person
Power of attorney of the filing agent, if applicable
Payment confirmation of RCS filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The RCS issues a formal query (réquisition) via the eService mailbox; respond with corrected or supplemented documents within 15 days. If registration is refused, re-file a rectified application or appeal to the District Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within two months of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish incorporation particulars in the RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically transmits the registration data to the RESA. Verify the published notice (name, legal form, registered office, partners' liability regime) on resa.lu and request correction without delay if any discrepancy is identified.
required_dossiers: No separate filing required; RCS registration data is forwarded ex officio
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request an ex officio corrective publication through the RCS; if the RESA entry is materially incorrect, the court may order a rectified notice upon application by the managing partner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain national business number and VAT registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) via the Guichet.lu / MyGuichet portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the RCS extract, file the VAT registration form electronically to obtain the national business number (numéro d'identification) and the Luxembourg VAT number. The SCSp is tax-transparent for income tax but is a separate VAT person if economically active. For EU distance sales of camping equipment, indicate the Union One-Stop-Shop (OSS) scheme; if the general partner is an entity, provide its corporate VAT details.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate (extract no older than 3 months)
Signed partnership agreement
Certificate or proof of registered office address
Identity documents of authorized signatories
Bank account details (IBAN) and proof of account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to AEDT requests through the MyGuichet electronic mailbox within the prescribed deadline; if documents are rejected, re-submit notarized or apostilled copies; apply for an EU VAT number and OSS registration if the authority requires a different procedure for cross-border sales.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with the social security authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) via the CondEploy / e-social-security platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp as an employer on the CCSS platform only when hiring employees. The managing partner who actively exercises management functions must be affiliated as a self-employed person (indépendant) unless affiliated through a corporate general partner. No registration is required for a purely passive SCSp without employees or active manager remuneration.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
Employment contracts of staff, if any
Identity documents and national registration numbers of directors and employees
Declaration of commencement of business activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify declarations directly with CCSS; if late registration triggers late-payment penalties, submit a written request for remission citing the RCS registration date as evidence of good faith.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for the business establishment permit (Autorisation d'établissement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy - Department for Commerce (Direction générale du commerce) via Guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Where the SCSp (or its managing partner) directly operates the retail e-commerce business from Luxembourg, submit an application for the autorisation d'établissement under the Law of 2 September 2011. Pure online trading without a physical shop open to the public may qualify for a simplified retail permit. Provide the criminal record of the natural-person manager and evidence of professional competence (diploma or three years of professional experience in retail).
required_dossiers: Establishment permit application form (completed online)
Extract of criminal record (casier judiciaire) of the natural-person manager
RCS extract and partnership agreement
Proof of professional qualification or managerial experience
Certificate of non-declaration of bankruptcy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is refused, request a discretionary review by the Minister of the Economy within three months of notification; a subsequent refusal may be challenged before the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg (Tribunal administratif).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open corporate bank account and activate payment rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg licensed credit institution (e.g., BNP Paribas Luxembourg, BCEE, ING, or a PSD2-licensed EMI); Stripe and PayPal onboarding teams
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the RCS extract and VAT certificate to open a corporate bank account. Because the SCSp lacks legal personality, the managing partner contracts and holds bank mandates in the partnership's name. Complete KYC/AML standard due diligence (low-risk retail). For Stripe and PayPal, submit the Luxembourg VAT number, partnership deed, and merchant website details; the payment rails are activated after bank account verification and merchant underwriting review.
required_dossiers: RCS extract (no older than 3 months)
Signed partnership agreement
Identity documents and personal statements of beneficial owners holding more than 25% of partnership interests
Certificate of good standing of the corporate general partner
Business plan and projected e-commerce volumes
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional KYC evidence, provide a sworn beneficial-ownership declaration and detailed source-of-funds statement; if local bank onboarding fails, engage a PSD2-licensed European EMI to obtain an IBAN and connect Stripe/PayPal, ensuring the merchant account is registered to the Luxembourg SCSp tax number.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy - Direction générale du commerce (General Department for Commerce); municipal (commune) authorities for warehouse and premises permitting
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) under the Law of 2 September 2011 on the Freedom of Establishment and Provision of Services, valid for retail and distance-selling activities; no sector-specific statutory license applies to outdoor camping equipment retail.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - online retail of camping goods is not listed in Annex I or Annex II of the Law of 22 May 2008 on Environmental Impact Assessment; no EIA report or registration is required for pure e-commerce operations. If a logistics warehouse exceeding 10,000 m² gross floor area is developed, a class 2 municipal land-use and environmental assessment procedure may apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams are generated by warehousing and online sales. General compliance applies: sanitary wastewater per the Law of 19 December 2008 on Water and the grand-ducal regulation of 30 November 2011; packaging waste obligations under the Law of 21 March 2017 on Packaging and the Valorlux scheme; household/municipal waste disposal rules under the Law of 21 March 2012 on Waste Management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: If physical premises (office/warehouse) are occupied: fire safety certification by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS), structural load compliance and occupancy permit from the municipal building authority (autorisation de bâtir), and workplace safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) under the Law of 17 June 1994 on Occupational Safety and Health. For a pure remote operation using third-party fulfillment, no fire-safety or occupational clearance is required beyond the registered-office occupancy compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT, via the MyGuichet.lu and eCDF portals.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first obtain a Luxembourg business registration number by registering with the Luxembourg Business Registers through MyGuichet.lu and filing the partnership deed with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés. The national TIN is then assigned by the ACD upon completion of tax registration. For VAT, a separate VAT identification number is applied for with the AEDT using form No. 1033/640/10 itself or electronically through MyGuichet.lu, which is mandatory prior to carrying out taxable supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An SCSp is fiscally transparent by default for Luxembourg income tax purposes, meaning income, gains, and losses are attributed directly to its partners. No general check-the-box election is available; however, if the SCSp carries on a commercial business with limited liability, Luxembourg optional solidarity tax and net wealth tax regimes may apply at the partnership level. For VAT, the SCSp may be treated as a separate taxable person, and a VAT grouping election under Article 62 of the Luxembourg VAT Law can be made.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for established taxable persons under the small-business exemption; however, a non-established seller is required to register for Luxembourg VAT immediately upon carrying out taxable supplies in the Grand Duchy, regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently mandate a nationwide real-time e-invoicing or fiscal clearance requirement for B2B supplies. Invoices must nevertheless contain all statutory VAT particulars, and for e-commerce/export purposes, electronic invoicing using PEPPOL-compliant formats is accepted. VAT returns must be filed electronically via the AEDT eCDF system, and the intra-EU OSS/WEB portal is obligatory for distance sales of goods to final consumers in Luxembourg where the Luxembourg turnover threshold is exceeded.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available where goods are physically dispatched or transported to a destination outside the European Union by the seller or on the seller's behalf, and ownership has passed to the non-EU buyer. For online sales of outdoor camping equipment shipped outside the EU, the supplier must retain evidence of transport outside the EU within the statutory export period. Services directly connected to goods temporarily or permanently exported attract zero-rating only if separately supported and within the Luxembourg VAT rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Electronic SAD through PLDA/ICS), Bill of Lading / CMR / AWB, Commercial Invoice, Proof of payment or bank remittance certificate, Contract or purchase order from non-EU customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where a Luxembourg VAT-registered person claims export zero-rating without substantive and reliable export documentation, the AEDT may retroactively assess VAT at 17%, plus late-payment interest at the monthly legal rate, and administrative fines of up to EUR 4,000 or a fixed multiplier of the evaded tax. Intentional suppression of export receipts or evidence, including false inward remittance certificates, is criminal fraud punishable under Article 92 of the Luxembourg VAT Law and may result in imprisonment, disqualification, and seizure of goods; an unjustified refund for zero-rated export supplies is recoverable with a claw-back of up to 10 years in cases of established fraudulent intent.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); banking conduct and AML/CFT supervision exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-area member and maintains no foreign-exchange controls. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully convertible under EU Treaty free-movement-of-capital rules and Luxembourg law. Profit remittances and partnership distributions to non-resident investors are not subject to exchange-control approval or forced conversion. A fiscally transparent SCSp is not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax on partnership distributions. Bank-level controls apply only to KYC, source-of-wealth, sanctions, and balance-of-payments statistical reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation timeline, or mandatory euro conversion ratio for export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency in an authorised bank account. Settlement data must be reported to the BCL for balance-of-payments statistics when the exporting entity meets direct reporting thresholds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE) / Spuerkeess
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account; Operational EUR Account
Operational Multi-Currency Account; Trade Finance / LC Account
Operational EUR/USD/CNH Account; FX Hedging Account
Operational Account; Correspondent Banking Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for EEA-authorised electronic money institutions and payment institutions passporting into Luxembourg under PSD2; Medium for UK, Swiss, or Asian digital banks operating through a Luxembourg agent or local authorisation; Low for unlicensed offshore EMIs because Luxembourg law requires CSSF authorisation or an EEA passport for holding payment accounts. Use EMIs and marketplaces such as Stripe and PayPal for e-commerce revenue collection, then concentrate funds to a tier-1 Luxembourg bank for disbursement, capital calls, escrow, and LC operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no blanket statutory requirement that directors or general partners appear physically in Luxembourg for SCSp account opening. CSSF-compliant remote onboarding using video identification and electronic signatures is permitted for low-risk structures. In practice, tier-1 banks often require the general partner or authorised manager to attend an initial KYC interview in Luxembourg or at a foreign branch. Required documents typically include the RCS excerpt, partnership agreement, UBO declaration, capital-call notice, source-of-funds profile, and notarised or apostilled authorisations where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity in the SCSp: limited partner identities and capital commitments are not publicly disclosed on the RCS, and the general partner may appear to control the vehicle without clear ownership evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised or legalised partnership agreement; RCS registration extract; filed UBO register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) confirmation; AML/legal opinion explaining SCSp governance; capital-call notices; identity and source-of-wealth file for the general partner and qualifying limited partners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated marketplace payment flows from Stripe, PayPal, Amazon, or other payment facilitators that make the underlying e-commerce sales ledger appear opaque to the bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment-processor settlement summaries; platform merchant agreements and user IDs; daily order-level transaction logs; refund and chargeback history; invoice and delivery records; automated sanctions and fraud-control output demonstrating no layering or unexplained third-party receipts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border trade disbursements to non-EU suppliers in USD or CNH without full commercial documentation, raising invoice-financing, transfer-pricing, or customs-valuation questions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed supply agreements, purchase orders, commercial invoices, bills of lading or airway bills, Incoterms, customs declarations, bank purpose codes, transfer-pricing or margin documentation, and supplier KYC files.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or high-risk-jurisdiction alerts linked to end-customers or third-party logistics providers in the outdoor-equipment retail channel.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time sanctions and PEP screening reports; IP and card-bank country data; geo-blocking policy; B2B customer KYC files; refusal-to-deal policy; suspicious-activity report logs where required; compliance attestation from payment processors.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 from each limited partner to the SCSp's dedicated account at a Luxembourg tier-1 bank, or MT202/COV where correspondent cover is needed. Reference each transfer to the signed capital-call notice and the partner's capital account. Use the BCL balance-of-payments statistical code for direct investment equity or shareholder loan, not goods or services, when reporting thresholds apply. Confirm the code with the receiving bank in advance. Funds may be credited in EUR, USD, CNH, or other freely convertible currencies without mandatory conversion; the source-of-funds dossier must accompany the first inbound credit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR supplier payments within the EEA and SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR or non-SEPA disbursements. For bulk or contract-manufacturing purchases, use an irrevocable documentary letter of credit transmitted via SWIFT MT700, with MT707 for amendments and compliant presentation under UCP600. For smaller trade payables, documentary collections (DP/DA) are acceptable. Commercial invoices, Incoterms, customs declarations, and LC terms must be aligned to the clearing instruction to avoid AML and trade-finance mismatches.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla EUR/USD FX forwards with maturities matched to commercial invoices and e-commerce cash-conversion cycles
Vanilla EUR/CNH FX forwards and FX swaps for operating-liquidity and settlement-date mismatches
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in CNH/USD or other restricted currencies where physical settlement is unavailable in the correspondent clearing corridor
Cross-currency swaps in EUR/USD and EUR/CNH for working-capital or term-debt hedging
Trade-related FX options only when executed through a CSSF-licensed Luxembourg credit institution and covered by an internal treasury risk policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (dépôt des comptes annuels) in abridged form for a small SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) through the lbr.lu e-filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven (7) months after the close of the financial year; for a calendar-year SCSp, no later than 31 July of the following year (accounts must be approved by the partners within six (6) months of the year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice issued by the RCS; criminal fine of EUR 500–25,000 against the defaulting general partner; verified non-deposit for two consecutive financial years allows compulsory deregistration (radiation d'office) after notice published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration of Conformity (déclaration annuelle de conformité) confirming that the RCS registration data of the SCSp remain accurate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), operated by LBR via lbr.lu
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one (1) month following each anniversary of the SCSp's RCS registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: RCS reminder and demand letter; failure to regularise within the three (3) month grace period exposes the SCSp to administrative strike-off proceedings and the criminal fines applicable under the RCS law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Beneficial Owners (confirmation annuelle au Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs / RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), maintained by LBR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one (1) month following the anniversary of the initial RBE declaration; a separate modification declaration is due within one (1) month of any change in the limited partners controlling the SCSp (e.g., transfer of partnership interests)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines of EUR 250–1,250 per natural-person general partner and up to EUR 1,250,000 for a corporate general partner; until regularisation, affected partners may not exercise voting rights or receive distributions under the UBO law.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) is triggered only where the SCSp exceeds two of the three thresholds at the balance-sheet date: (i) balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, (ii) net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, or (iii) average workforce above 50 full-time employees. Sub-threshold SCSp may remain unaudited unless the partnership agreement or limited partners holding at least 10% of the capital rights request an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg statutory GAAP set by the Law of 19 December 2020 on annual and consolidated accounts (transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU); EU-endorsed IFRS permitted for consolidated financial statements. A qualifying small SCSp may file an abridged balance sheet and abridged explanatory notes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner(s) must confirm annually, via the LBR RBE portal, that the beneficial-owner information is exact and current within one (1) month of the anniversary of the initial RBE filing. Any transfer of limited-partnership interests which changes beneficial ownership (direct or indirect control exceeding 25% of interests, voting rights, or ultimate ownership) requires an RBE modification declaration within one (1) month of the change and a simultaneous update of the SCSp's register of limited partners.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Register of Limited Partners / registre des associés commanditaires)
Register of General Partner(s) and Authorised Managers (dirigeants) of the SCSp
Minute Book of Partner Decisions (procès-verbaux des décisions des associés)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – USD 4,500 per annum for a Luxembourg registered office/domiciliation, statutory correspondence handling, and RCS compliance agent services of a low-risk e-commerce retail SCSp
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 – USD 13,000 for a certified statutory audit of a small-to-medium SCSp under Luxembourg GAAP; the engagement is voluntary below the statutory audit thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined CIT 17% + municipal business tax ~6.75% + solidarity surcharge 7% on CIT)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), investment tax credit, notional interest deduction (NID) for equity financing

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1000 (Corporate Income Tax Return) and Form 1001 (Municipal Business Tax Return) filed via eCaisse (electronic filing system)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 31 May of the year following the fiscal year end; extensions up to 6 months may be granted upon request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the taxpayer (name, address, RCS number, fiscal year)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Luxembourg tax identification number and permanent establishment details if applicable
Report only Luxembourg-source income attributable to the permanent establishment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and exemptions (e.g., IP box, NID, tax credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only deductions directly related to Luxembourg-source income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computation (CIT, municipal business tax, solidarity surcharge)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate taxes based on Luxembourg taxable base; no foreign tax credit unless treaty provision

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of EUR 10 to EUR 2,500, plus daily interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid tax, capped at 10% of total tax due

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if holding ≥10% for 12 months)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, submit Form 22 (withholding tax exemption) to Luxembourg tax authorities, provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the recipient's jurisdiction, and apply for reduced rate before dividend payment
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not impose withholding tax on royalties and interest, except for certain cases (e.g., excessive interest to non-residents). Treaty rates may apply if any.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 1,000,000 for related party transactions (Local File); group revenue > EUR 50 million for Master File
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to entities engaged in relevant activities; for retail trading, substance is required based on actual operations, employees, and management in Luxembourg.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income, false invoicing, or artificial transfer pricing arrangements to shift profits to low-tax jurisdictions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to EUR 250,000 or 100% of evaded tax, plus criminal prosecution; tax reassessment with interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 5 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Lack of economic substance (no physical office, no employees, no real business activity) while claiming tax benefits or treaty relief
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, retroactive tax assessment, penalty up to EUR 50,000, and potential dissolution of entity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for unpaid taxes, travel bans, and disqualification from directorship

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement anti-money laundering controls, suspicious transaction reporting, or due diligence on customers (e.g., accepting cash payments without verification)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to EUR 1 million or 10% of annual turnover; criminal sanctions for money laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be subject to imprisonment up to 5 years, personal fines, and travel bans
